2 min read


By[Anthony DeFino](https://www.healio.com/authors/adefino)

## Key takeaways:


- There were no reported cases of ocular serious adverse events.
- Best corrected visual acuity improved by a mean of 10.8 letters.


In part one of the SPECTRA clinical trial, 4D-150, an intravitreal gene therapy, demonstrated positive safety outcomes as well as vision gains and central subfield thickness reduction in patients with[diabetic macular edema](https://www.healio.com/news/ophthalmology/20260925/remigromig-meets-endpoint-in-phase-2b3-diabetic-macular-edema-trial) .


“For DME patients, the current treatment paradigm requires time-consuming retinal clinic visits and anti-VEGF injections every 4 to 8 weeks,” **Arshad Khanani, MD, MA, FASRS,** chair of 4D Molecular Therapeutics’ retina advisory board, told Healio. “This is on top of other regular physician visits needed to control their diabetes. Because of this rigorous schedule, many patients struggle to adhere to their treatment regimen, which may lead to suboptimal visual outcomes. The 2-year data from the SPECTRA clinical trial give me hope that a single in-office injection of 4D-150 has the potential to transform the treatment paradigm for DME by providing sustained disease control while reducing treatment burden.”


According to a press release from 4DMT, safety was evaluated in 22 patients with DME. The gene therapy was well tolerated, with no reported ocular serious adverse events or intraocular inflammation, hypotony, endophthalmitis, vasculitis, choroidal effusions or retinal artery occlusions. In addition, there was no progression to proliferative diabetic retinopathy or vitreous hemorrhage, according to the release.


“Previous intravitreal gene therapy for DME led to serious adverse events that impacted patients’ vision,” Khanani told Healio. “The SPECTRA study, however, showed zero cases of inflammation reported, which is encouraging as phase 3 enrollment in the 4SIGHT clinical trial has begun.”


Nine patients received the phase 3 dose of 3E10 vg/eye of 4D-150. In this group, there was a mean increase in best corrected visual acuity of 10.8 letters and a mean reduction in central subfield thickness of 176 µm. After three loading doses of aflibercept, patients experienced a 61% overall treatment burden reduction, with a mean of 5.2 supplemental injections per patient vs. a projected 13 injections with on-label aflibercept 2 mg dosed every 8 weeks.


Of the nine patients, 22% remained injection-free, according to the release.


4DMT announced patient enrollment for the 4SIGHT phase 3 clinical trial, which will continue evaluating the gene therapy for treatment of DME. The primary endpoint is noninferiority to aflibercept 2 mg in mean change from baseline in BCVA at week 52 in 514 patients, each of whom will receive five aflibercept loading doses, according to the release.


“The favorable safety profile observed through 2 years in the SPECTRA part one clinical trial in DME is what I find most significant,” Khanani told Healio. “I look forward to supporting 4DMT with its phase 3 4SIGHT trial to bring this potential paradigm-shifting treatment to patients in need.”


The FDA granted regenerative medicine advanced therapy designation to 4D-150 for DME in May 2025,[as Healio previously reported](https://www.healio.com/news/ophthalmology/20250502/fda-grants-regenerative-medicine-advanced-therapy-designation-to-4d150-in-dme) .
